# Gaps backlog

Generated by running `skills/harvest-gaps-from-lessons-learned` (spec.md
§11.2) for real against the full 24-use-case corpus — task 9.4, not a
single-document dry run. Every use case's `## Lessons learned`/`## Impacts
identified` sections were read (21 of 24 carry both; TMFS009 has neither;
TMFS018 nests "Impacts identified" under "Lessons learned" rather than as
a sibling — all checked directly against the live corpus before writing
this, not assumed). Enhancement requests to existing APIs (the majority of
what's in these sections — field/attribute/operation additions, mostly
tracked as individual `AP-xxxx`/`ISA-xxxx` JIRA tickets) are deliberately
excluded per the skill's own Step 2 filter: this file is about capability
gaps — proposed components/APIs that don't exist at all yet — not a JIRA
export.

Cross-checked against `knowledge/index/components.json`/`apis.json` as of
this run (24 use cases, 31 components, 51 API versions, same corpus as
`spec/tasks.md` Phase 4): **none of the five gaps below have been
resolved since the citing use cases were written.** Re-run this
cross-check on every future refresh cycle — a gap here can go stale the
same way TMFS030 itself already reports one of its own smaller
observations did (a Product Configurator gap resolved by TMFC027 v2.2.0,
noted directly in that document's own text).

## 1. API exposure / gateway component for B2B boundary translation

**Status: still open. No `TMFCxxx`/`TMFxxx` id assigned anywhere.**

Raised independently, in different words, by **four** different use
cases — the strongest corroboration signal in this backlog:

| Use case | How it's raised |
|---|---|
| TMFS018 | `BuyerGW`/`SellerGW` concept; tracked as `TAC-841` "Wholesale Broadband Gateway," status "pending information" per the document |
| TMFS021 | States existing sequence diagrams don't include any exposure layer, though "in real world scenarios security is to be ensured" — no ticket cited |
| TMFS026 | Introduces "Open Gateway Façade," a translation component between standardized APIs (TMF931, TMF936) and internal ODA components (TMF620, TMF622, TMF632, TMF639, TMF669) |
| TMFS030 | Most mature articulation: formalizes a proposed **"Delegate Component" type** — exposes/protects/adapts TMF Open APIs at the ODA boundary, applies Proxy/Decorator patterns, handles security/policy/throttling/auditing without altering business semantics. Cites a named Accelerate 2026 concept proposal (Kamal Maghsoudlou) and an open action item to "consolidate definitions (canonical, aggregated, composite, delegate, AI-powered, AI-native) into a unified taxonomy" |

TMFS030 also names **TMFS007** ("B2B use-case re-using MEF") as a fifth
case that would benefit from this — TMFS007 is `planned` in IG1228, not
yet converted into this corpus (`knowledge/index/usecase-list.json`), so
its own framing of the gap couldn't be read directly for this run.

## 2. Business Partner / Supplier-side order management

**Status: still open. No ids assigned to any of the four proposed new assets.**

| Use case | How it's raised |
|---|---|
| TMFS020 | Primary source — three named alternatives considered (new dedicated components vs. extending existing TMFC002/TMFC003 vs. a hybrid reusing `TMFC033` Purchase Management). Proposes: `TMFCxxx Business Partner Order Capture & Validation`, `TMFCxxx Business Partner Order Delivery Orchestration and Management`, `TMFxxx Procurement Request API`, `TMFxxx Supplier Order API`. Tracked: `TAC-1387`, `TAC-1388`, `TAC-1390`, all "backlog" as of writing |
| TMFS030 | Reinforces the same gap, explicitly cross-referencing TMFS020's proposal and TMFS007's independent framing of a "Purchase Management" recipient role |

Related but distinct: `TMFC033` "Purchase Management" already has an
assigned id and is cached with `status: "not_yet_specified"` in
`knowledge/index/components.json` — a **later** pipeline stage than the
four fully-unassigned proposals above. TMFS020/TMFS030 both discuss
*extending or decomposing* TMFC033 as an alternative to introducing the
brand-new components, not as something already resolving the gap.

## 3. Dedicated Resource Reservation component

**Status: still open. No id assigned.**

Raised only by TMFS030: "Currently, there are no ODA components exposing
the TMF716 Resource Reservation API" (the API itself *is* cached in
`knowledge/apis/TMF716/` — this is a gap in component coverage, not API
coverage). Candidates discussed: extending `TMFC012` Resource Inventory
or `TMFC011` Resource Order Management, or introducing a new dedicated
component. Tracked: `TAC-1389` "Create and Publish: TMFCxxx New ODA
Component for Resource Reservation and Allocation," "backlog" as of
writing.

## 4. Fallout / exception-handling component (order & process orchestration)

**Status: open per the citing documents' own text as of their writing; live ticket status not independently verifiable from this corpus.**

| Use case | How it's raised |
|---|---|
| TMFS011 | Most detailed source — explicitly states "a new Open API should also be defined... as well as SID entities to maintain its information structures," describing required capabilities (listen across components for failures, act against any component/interface, configurable auto/manual resolution). Suggests placement in the Intelligence Management functional block |
| TMFS008 | Independently cites the *same* ticket — `TAC-280` "Service & Resource Orchestration" — as the tracking item for this need |

The shared `TAC-280` citation across two independently-written use cases
is the corroboration signal here, not prose similarity alone. No id
assigned to either a component or API for this capability yet.

## 5. SID gap, noted but not cross-checked (`knowledge/sid/` is empty)

`SoftwareSupportPackageSpec` missing in SID — raised only by TMFS025,
tracked as `ISA-1131`, "backlog" as of writing. `knowledge/sid/` is
reserved but unpopulated (spec.md §7), so this can't be cross-checked
against a local corpus the way components/APIs can. Logged for
completeness, not verified against current SID state.

## Deliberately excluded from this backlog

The large majority of "Lessons learned"/"Impacts identified" content
across the corpus is enhancement requests to *existing* APIs — new
fields, new operations, clarified attributes — each usually its own
`AP-xxxx`/`ISA-xxxx` ticket. That's real, valuable feedback for API
maintainers, but it's evolution of something that already exists, not a
missing asset, and there are far too many individual instances across 21
documents to aggregate into one backlog without drowning the five genuine
new-capability gaps above in noise. If a consumer needs the full,
unfiltered list for a specific API, read that use case's own "Impacts
identified" section directly.
